routes.line: Citranet (AS23951), the Solo internet company behind Citranet DC Surakarta and CitraIX Surakarta
routes.story: Two hops inside Solo on Citranet, two in Jakarta on FiberStar, then across the sea to Singapore, where FiberStar hands the message to Vultr at Equinix’s exchange.
routes.label: Citranet, from Solo

hops.how: The test device’s gateway, the first router on its line. Globalping puts the device in Surakarta.
The router’s name ends in solo.citra.net.id.
hops.name: solo.citra.net.id

hops.how: 10 ms there and back: too far for Semarang or Surabaya, about right for Jakarta. FiberStar carries Citranet’s traffic, and both have equipment in four Greater Jakarta buildings on this map (Gedung Cyber 1, IDC 3D, DCI Indonesia and Equinix JK1 Jakarta), so we can’t say which one.
Same delay as hop 3.
Same delay as hop 6, which is in Singapore. The 14 ms jump since hop 4 is the trip across the sea.
Its address belongs to Equinix’s internet exchange in Singapore (router name …sgw.equinix.com). FiberStar hands the message to Vultr here.
hops.name: sgw.equinix.com

hops.how: A private address inside Vultr’s own network.
Answered slowly. Busy routers reply to tests late; hop 9 answers in 24 ms, so the road itself is not slower.
Vultr’s Singapore network.
hops.name: 32.98.222.vultrusercontent.com

hops.how: The destination: Vultr’s Singapore test server.
hops.name: vultr.com

routes.line: Telkomsel (AS23693), likely an IndiHome line: 3 ms to Telkom’s first router is fibre speed. Telkom’s own network carries it
routes.story: Three hops inside the house, two in Yogyakarta on Telkom, then one jump to Telin’s Singapore network: the road through Jakarta never shows. Telkom hands the message to Vultr at the Singapore Internet Exchange.
routes.label: Telkomsel, from Yogyakarta

hops.how: Inside the test device itself.
A router in the house.
The home modem.
3 ms: Telkom’s local network, close by (a private address).
Telkom’s first public router, still 3 ms away.
Its address is registered to Telin’s Singapore network. 20 ms in one jump: the road through Jakarta stays inside Telkom’s network and doesn’t show.
Same delay as hop 6.
Its address belongs to the Singapore Internet Exchange (SGIX). Telkom hands the message to Vultr here.

routes.line: XL (AS139994 for the line, AS24203 for its backbone), a home connection
routes.story: One hop in the house, two on XL’s network where the data gives no place, then XL’s own port at Equinix’s exchange in Singapore. The fewest hops, but the slowest: the first jump alone takes 17 ms.
routes.label: XL, from Sleman

hops.how: The home router.
17 ms on the first jump: XL’s access line plus distance. Nothing in the data says where this router is (a private address).
Same delay as hop 2.
XL’s own port at Equinix’s internet exchange in Singapore (router name 24203.sgw.equinix.com).
hops.name: sgw.equinix.com

hops.how: Vultr’s port at the same exchange, where XL hands the message over. It answered slowly.
